class.name: BulletEffectLayerData2D
class.brief_description: One stackable sprite-effect layer for a bullet volley: a trail that follows bullets, or a one-shot visual (spawn flash, hit sparks, destroy explosion, bounce sparks).
class.description: Put layers in [MultiMeshBulletsData2D.effect_layers] — as many as you want. Each layer renders through its own per-frame shards (one extra draw call per animation frame while anything is visible, zero when idle), so layers never fight each other and every instance can show a different animation frame. Upload [member sprite_frames] per layer (a layer with null frames is inert). Use [BulletAttachment2D] scenes instead when you need particles or scripted nodes; use layers for plain sprites. One texture per layer is shared by all its instances (the performance bargain), so per-bullet different textures are not supported — vary instances with [member random_start_frame], [member randomize_rotation], [member random_scale_min]/[member random_scale_max] and [member trigger_chance] instead. Tint with [member self_modulate], or over life with [member color_ramp]. Bakes are snapshots: editing a layer's frames mid-life does not refresh live volleys or factory bakes — call [method MultiMeshBullets2D.set_effect_layers] (or [method MultiMeshBullets2D.play_effect_animation] for trails) to apply edits.

members.member: Which animation to play. Empty or "default" auto-resolves silently: "default" if present, else the first animation with frames. Switch a live trail layer with [method MultiMeshBullets2D.play_effect_animation].

Tint-over-life ramp, sampled per instance by animation age (one-shots) or loop phase (trails), exactly like particle color ramps. Multiplies with [member self_modulate]. Null (default) keeps every instance solid. Example: white-to-transparent red ramp on a destroy layer fades each explosion out individually.
Master switch: toggle a layer without removing it from the array.
Light mask bitmask for this layer's shards (same numbering as the bullet light_mask). Lets effects opt out of 2D lights.
Per-layer material override. Null renders with default blending.

One-shot slot ring size: the oldest slot is recycled past this. Bounds worst-case memory per layer. 0 (default) means auto: max(32, 2x the spawning volley's bullet count), so one effect per bullet plus margin with zero config (the manual hatch without a volley falls back to 64). Trail layers ignore it (one slot per bullet by construction).
Trail follow offset from the bullet origin, rotated with the bullet. One-shots add it (rotated by the event orientation) to the event pose.
Upper end of the random uniform scale range per fired one-shot slot. Must stay finite and above [member random_scale_min].
Lower end of the random uniform scale range per fired one-shot slot. (1, 1) disables the randomization.

Desync: one-shot slots start at a random animation age, trail bullets at a random loop phase. Same-frame kills then read as a volley, not a slideshow copy. Off by default so timing stays exact unless asked.
Spin each fired one-shot slot randomly (full 360). Ideal for spark bursts.

Static visual rotation in degrees, applied on top of the bullet or event orientation (a 90-degree streak flies sideways to its bullet). Positive spins clockwise. Example: rotation_degrees 90 on a trail turns a forward streak into a sideways ribbon.
Uniform visual scale of the layer (multiplies the frame size).
Layer-wide tint, exactly like CanvasItem self_modulate (multiplies every instance of this layer). White renders the art untouched.

Continuous spin in degrees per second (pinwheels, rotating sparks, shimmering trails). 0 (default) disables it. Signed: negative spins counter-clockwise. Derived from the running clock, so pooled reuse never desyncs it. Example: spin_degrees_per_sec 180 turns a trail glow one half-turn per second.
Frames to play (required: null frames leave the layer inert with a single bake-time warning, never a crash).

What this layer does: 0 Trail Follow (sticks to its bullet every tick, and follows physics interpolation exactly like the bullet), 1 On Spawn (muzzle flash at every bullet's spawn pose), 2 On Hit (sparks on counted hits), 3 On Destroy (explosion on collision-kill only, never on lifetime expiry or manual disable), 4 On Bounce (sparks on ricochet; a consumed bounce fires this once, not the hit spark), 5 On Lifetime Over (fizzle at expiry, on both the silent and the signalled expiry path).
Fire probability per event. Stack three explosion layers at 0.5 and every kill looks different. 0 never fires, 1 always fires.
Visibility layer bitmask for this layer's shards (same numbering as the bullet visibility_layer). Lets effects render on chosen canvases.

Whether [member z_index] is relative. Trail shards are children of the volley, so relative offsets track the volley z forever. One-shot shards live under the factory, where the offset behaves like an absolute z.
Draw order of this layer's shards. Default +1 renders above the bullets; use -1 for glows and shadows beneath them.

constants.constant: Trail layer: follows its bullet every tick, dies with it.
One-shot fired at every bullet's spawn pose on spawn and pool-pop (never on pre-population or single-bullet wakes).
One-shot fired on counted hits (never on free bounces, never twice on a consumed bounce).
One-shot fired on collision-kill only (never on lifetime expiry or manual disable, and never together with the hit spark).
One-shot fired on every ricochet (directional volleys only).
One-shot fired at each bullet's death pose on lifetime expiry (both the silent and the signalled path), even as the volley pools underneath it.
